body.statement: There is an interval specified by \(def:robust-heavy-light-interval-handle\) such that, for every \(d\le c_{\epsilon}n\log(en)\), \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}Q_P^{(n)}\{\tau(P)\in\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}\}\ge1-\alpha\) and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[|\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}|]\lesssim_{\epsilon,\alpha}r_{n,d,M}\). The guarantee uses only the observed sample, the known values \(M\), \(\epsilon\), and \(\alpha\), and the conditions defining \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\).
body.justification: The corrected handle exposes the intended sample split and all-heavy identity but does not claim unproved radii.
body.gap: Both the selected-factorial light radius and the winsorized Gaussian/fallback heavy radius lack explicit valid sample maps and tail theorems.
body.consumer: The intended consumer is a uniformly valid replacement for the reference intervals in the Zeng et al. 401(k) analysis.

obligation.what_is_open: Finite-sample coverage and the sharp expected-radius bound for an explicit heavy--light interval on the unrestricted global class.
obligation.obstruction: The selected-factorial rare radius remains unresolved in the sibling-owned rare-tail question, and the heavy winsorized Gaussian/fallback radius is still not an explicit sample map. The exact all-heavy center and variance override does not furnish either tail certificate.
obligation.attempted: I combined the proved light-branch bias with the exact all-heavy override and decomposed the remaining error into light fluctuation, heavy fluctuation, truncation, and pilot terms. Only the deterministic light bias and the local all-heavy bridge follow from the frozen primitives.
obligation.partial_result:
The proved light-approximation lemma supplies
\[
 \left|E\widehat T_{\mathrm L}
 -E\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}}
 p_k(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k})\right|
 \le C_\epsilon M\frac{d}{n\log(en)}.
\]
The frozen heavy--light handle also gives an exact center and variance
identity on the all-heavy pilot event.  If explicit light and heavy radii
satisfied their allocated conditional tail bounds and had expected sizes
\(C_{\epsilon,\alpha}M\{n^{-1/2}+d/[n\log(en)]\}\) and
\(C_{\epsilon,\alpha}Mn^{-1/2}\), respectively, the triangle inequality and
the allocation of the noncoverage probability would prove the target, and
intersection with \([-2M,2M]\) would not enlarge length.  The frozen core
does not define radii with those properties, so this implication cannot be
turned into a proof of the stated interval theorem.
